subject: Marketplace renewal: acceptance timing & burst capacity synchronization
messages:
From: Elaine Chu <elaine@medstreamhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Josh Kramer <josh.kramer@cloudmarketplace.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & planned capacity increase — syncing acceptance window

Hi Ben,

Quick note as we ramp into our July workload: MedStream is planning to increase committed GPU capacity by ~35% starting 2026-07-15 to support a new image-processing pipeline. We want to accept the AWS Private Offer this month but need to make sure the marketplace acceptance window + invoice cutover aligns with our fiscal calendar and the burst capacity on day one.

Questions:
- Can Redwood align the acceptance (private offer acceptance via AWS) for 2026-07-10 to allow a clean billing cutover on 7/15?
- Is there a short-term burst capacity (30 days) you can provision immediately after acceptance while our Dedicated pool autoscale rules are adjusted?
- We will need a PO (PO_02459) routed for net-30. Any paperwork or signature sequencing we should follow?

Attaching a spreadsheet with requested start dates and invoice preferences.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Chu
Head of Cloud Ops, MedStream Health
Attachments: Private_Offer_Schedule.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chu <elaine@medstreamhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Josh Kramer <josh.kramer@cloudmarketplace.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & planned capacity increase — syncing acceptance window

Hi Elaine — thanks for the heads up and the spreadsheet, that’s helpful. High-level response before I loop legal and billing:

- Acceptance window: We can target private-offer acceptance on the 2026-07-10 date you requested. AWS typically processes the private offer acceptance within 24–48 hours, but we should leave a 72-hour buffer for marketplace propagation.
- Burst capacity: We can stand up a temporary burst pool for 30 days post-acceptance. I’ll need to confirm exact GPU types and cost for the burst; we can do a short addendum that covers the 30-day burst at an agreed uplift rate.
- PO flow: Net-30 is fine. Karthik — can you confirm our invoicing cadence if the private offer is accepted on 7/10 and effective on 7/15? Also looping Marissa for legal on the addendum language and any acceptance sequencing that impacts the PO.

Next steps:
1) Karthik and Marissa review and confirm billing/terms by EOD Wed 6/3.
2) I’ll draft a short acceptance timeline and a 30-day burst addendum we can attach to the PO/DocuSign package.
3) Elaine, please confirm final signature authority and whether MedStream wants Redwood to sign first or for you to sign via AWS directly.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Chu <elaine@medstreamhealth.com>, Josh Kramer <josh.kramer@cloudmarketplace.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & planned capacity increase — syncing acceptance window

Ben / Marissa — quick billing note:

- If MedStream accepts the private offer on 2026-07-10 and the effective date is 2026-07-15, we will pro-rate the first invoice to reflect the partial month (7/15–7/31) unless MedStream requests full-month billing. Net-30 terms apply from the invoice date.
- For the 30-day burst: recommend we invoice the burst as a separate line item dated the acceptance effective date so there’s no mingling with committed capacity invoices. That makes reporting easier for both sides.

Marissa — please confirm whether the addendum needs to reference a separate SOW or can be a one-page attachment to the private offer.

Karthik
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Elaine Chu <elaine@medstreamhealth.com>
Cc: Josh Kramer <josh.kramer@cloudmarketplace.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & planned capacity increase — syncing acceptance window

Elaine / team — legal ok on the approach; suggested flow below to avoid acceptance/contract sequencing issues with AWS marketplace:

1) Redwood prepares the one-page burst addendum (definition of burst, GPU SKU(s), uplift %, billing line item nomenclature).
2) MedStream issues PO_02459 referencing the private offer ID and the burst addendum. PO should state ‘acceptance subject to AWS Private Offer ID XXXXX’.
3) Redwood executes addendum and returns for signature.
4) MedStream accepts private offer in AWS and uploads signed addendum to the DocuSign link.

We recommend Redwood sign the addendum first to ensure the burst terms are locked — otherwise AWS may surface the private offer before both parties have executed addendum language and that can create invoice mismatch risk.

I’ll draft a one-page addendum and share a redline by EOD Thu 6/4.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chu <elaine@medstreamhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Josh Kramer <josh.kramer@cloudmarketplace.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & planned capacity increase — syncing acceptance window

Thanks everyone — Elaine, confirming next steps on our side and deliverables:

- I will upload the draft one-page burst addendum and the signed-private-offer checklist to the DocuSign package and share the link by EOD Thu 6/4. (Attachments: Private_Offer_Acceptance_Form.pdf)
- Karthik will prepare invoice line-item guidance and confirm whether Redwood will pro-rate or bill full month (we are set to pro-rate unless MedStream asks otherwise).
- Marissa will send the redline for the addendum; Ben will get legal-signed copy back to Elaine prior to pushing private-offer acceptance.

Elaine — please confirm: 1) who will sign on MedStream’s behalf (name + title), and 2) do you want Redwood to sign first as Marissa recommended? If yes, we will sign and return the DocuSign envelope, then ask you to complete acceptance in AWS once you have your PO attached.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — target: complete signatures and acceptance by 2026-07-10 so we can enable burst on 7/15.

Best,
Ben
Attachments: Private_Offer_Acceptance_Form.pdf, PO_02459.pdf
